comparator.name: Media Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 TER defines the redesigned 180-EC programme for students starting on 1 September 2026: 60 EC in each year. The pathway below uses the first-listed option wherever the regulations require a choice: Stories We Live By in Year 1, Technology and Creative Destruction and Global Change in Year 2, and Content Creation in Year 3. The three unnamed 5-EC thematic specializations are a single restricted-choice slot, preserved without inventing a specialization name. No formal route is defined.
components: Stories We Live By faculty-wide course
Professional Writing: From Page to Platform
One of three regulated thematic specializations; exact names are not supplied in the TER.
Media Careers: Prospects in the Market

alternatives.label: Media, Culture and Society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres media theory, history, platforms, representation, audiences and production in their cultural and social contexts, with communication and research support.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines film and media analysis, media history and platforms, representation, audiences, rhetoric, creative communication, literature, sociology, history, ethics and qualitative research. It captures the programme's comparative social and cultural identity without claiming its dedicated media-methods and professional sequence.
progression: Media, communication, literature, history, sociology, psychology and qualitative-methods foundations precede advanced media representation, documentary, persuasion, creative communication, social theory and independent research. All formal prerequisites and semester offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Media Industries, Communication and Audiences
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule combines media and communication with audience psychology, economics, marketing, organisations, digital transformation and market research.
alternatives.concept: A cultural-industries direction studying media organisations, audiences, markets, strategy, production and public communication through media studies, sociology, psychology, economics, marketing, leadership, digital transformation and applied audience research.
progression: Business, economics, sociology, rhetoric, psychology, media and research foundations precede cultural-industry strategy, media production, audience research, persuasion and organisational analysis. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Microeconomics & Behavior and Market Research. All offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from the closest match by 12 courses through economics, business, audience research, marketing, leadership and organisational strategy, well above the 30-EC floor.

alternatives.label: Digital Media, Data and Responsible AI
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule combines media and communication with programming, data science, machine learning, AI ethics, digital strategy and advanced AI decision systems.
alternatives.concept: A digital-cultures direction examining media platforms, datafication, algorithmic systems and communication through media analysis, programming, data science, machine learning, responsible AI, digital transformation and audience research.
progression: Programming, mathematics, data, media, psychology and methods foundations precede machine learning, digital-media analysis, deep learning, persuasion, audience research and AI decision systems. All formal prerequisites and semester offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs substantially from both prior alternatives through sustained programming, mathematics, data science, machine learning, AI ethics and computational decision-making; pairwise differences exceed 30 EC.

selection.assessment: The closest alternative owns the broad media, society, audiences, history, representation and visual-culture evidence. Cultural Industries and Digital Cultures then yield two coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct alternatives in programme-interest order. Journalism Studies and Politics and Global Citizenship remain evidenced candidates but are not attempted after the three-alternative maximum. Curricular-topic, illustrative and outcome rows support the mapped concepts but do not independently generate further alternatives.

blocks: Media theory, history and everyday life
Media Archaeology studies historical media technologies, material forms and cultural memory.
Introduction to Film & Media provides foundational analysis of media form, representation, narrative and technology.
Introduction to Sociology situates media practices in institutions, identities and everyday social relations.
Literary interpretation supports the selected stories-and-identity theme.
Social Psychology examines attitudes, groups, social cognition and audience influence.
Rhetorical Communication develops audience-aware argument and public writing.
Qualitative Research Methodology develops observation, interviewing and interpretation of social meaning.
No single scheduled UCR course reproduces the dedicated digital-futures design unit; related design and digital work is distributed across the alternatives.
Media analysis, power, representation and research
The Documentary combines media analysis, production choices, evidence and ethics.
Advanced social theory examines power, trust and public life.
Media & Race studies representation, storytelling, identity and power.
From T.V. to TikTok examines platforms and mediated social narratives.
Strategy & Digital Transformation examines organisational change driven by digital technologies.
Media & the Environment addresses the selected global-change theme through media framing of collective problems.
History Research Seminar supplies independent source-based research and academic argument.
Film & Text provides a coherent thematic specialization in relationships between textual and audiovisual narratives.
Media industries, audiences and professional practice
Business Foundations introduces creative ventures, market validation and collaborative project work.
Research Methods & Statistics develops survey, experimental and quantitative evaluation.
Digital media, data and responsible AI
AI Ethics provides critical frameworks for fairness, privacy, accountability and human interaction with algorithmic media.
Open curriculum, content creation and thesis
The 30-EC minor is genuine open space; the complete UCR schedules are examples rather than substitutions.
Creative Communication Laboratory is the strongest content-creation counterpart.
Groningen requires a 10-EC Media Studies thesis; UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

notes.text: Groningen offers an integrated media-studies sequence in audiences, media use and production, archives, platforms, advanced methods, content creation, professional practice and a thesis. UCR offers strong related liberal-arts pathways but does not reproduce that dedicated sequence.
The 2026-2027 regulations introduce a redesigned curriculum for September 2026 starters. Transitional packages for earlier cohorts were not used.
